metadata.title: Communication-Efficient Algorithms for Statistical Optimization
metadata.authors: Yuchen Zhang, John C. Duchi, Martin J. Wainwright

nodes.name: Population risk
nodes.statement: Given a $\statprob$-integrable loss family $f(\cdot;x)$, the population risk is $F_0(\theta) \defeq \E_\statprob[f(\theta; X)] = \int f(\theta;x)\,d\statprob(x)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The expected loss under the data distribution.

nodes.name: Local empirical objective and distribution
nodes.statement: For processor $i$ with subset $S_{1,i}$ of size $n$: $\statprob_{1,i} \defeq \frac{1}{|S_{1,i}|}\sum_{x \in S_{1,i}} \delta_x$ and $F_{1,i}(\theta) \defeq \frac{1}{|S_{1,i}|}\sum_{x \in S_{1,i}} f(\theta; x)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Local empirical distribution and risk on processor $i$.

nodes.name: Fisher information matrix
nodes.statement:
$I(	heta^*) \defeq \E[
abla \log p(X \mid 	heta^*)
abla \log p(X \mid 	heta^*)^	op] = \E[
abla^2 \log p(X \mid 	heta^*)]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard Fisher information matrix for a parametric family.
nodes.origin_citation: Lehmann & Casella, Theory of Point Estimation, 1998

nodes.name: Asymptotic variance $\sigma^2$
nodes.statement: $\sigma^2 \defeq \E[\ltwo{\nabla^2 F_0(\theta^*)^{-1}\nabla f(\theta^*; X)}^2]$, the asymptotic variance of the inverse-Hessian-scaled gradient at $\theta^*$.
nodes.statement_clean: Inverse-Hessian-weighted gradient variance at the optimum.

nodes.name: Good events $\event_0,\event_1,\event_2$
nodes.statement_clean: Three high-probability events under which $F_1$ behaves like $F_0$ near $\theta^*$.

nodes.name: Empirical risk minimization (ERM)
nodes.statement: Estimate $\theta^* = \arg\min_{\theta \in \Theta} F_0(\theta)$ by solving $\widehat{\theta} \in \arg\min_{\theta \in \Theta} \frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{x \in S} f(\theta;x)$ given an i.i.d. sample $S$ from $\statprob$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the average loss over a sample to estimate the population minimizer.

nodes.name: Distributed/communication-efficient statistical optimization
nodes.statement: Given $N = mn$ samples split across $m$ machines, estimate $\theta^* = \arg\min_\theta F_0(\theta)$ using only a single round (or limited rounds) of inter-machine communication, matching the centralized rate $\sigma^2/N$ when possible.
nodes.statement_clean: Estimate the population risk minimizer from data spread over $m$ machines with minimal communication.

nodes.name: Click-through-rate logistic regression on Tencent SoSo data
nodes.statement: Predict click probability $P(y=1\mid x;\theta) = 1/(1+\exp(-\langle\theta,x\rangle))$ on $N \approx 2.4\times 10^8$ samples in $d \approx 7.4 \times 10^5$ dimensions by minimizing $f(\theta;(x,y)) = \log(1+\exp(-y\langle\theta,x\rangle)) + \frac{\lambda}{2}\ltwo{\theta}^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Large-scale ridge-regularized logistic regression for ad-click prediction on the Tencent dataset.

nodes.name: Parameters (compact convex domain)
nodes.statement: $\Theta \subset \R^d$ is compact and convex, $\theta^* \in \mathrm{int}(\Theta)$, and the $\ell_2$-radius is $R = \max_{\theta \in \Theta} \ltwo{\theta - \theta^*}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Parameter space is a bounded convex set containing the optimum in its interior.

nodes.name: Local strong convexity
nodes.statement: $F_0$ is twice differentiable and there exists $\lambda > 0$ such that $\nabla^2 F_0(\theta^*) \succeq \lambda I_{d \times d}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The population risk has positive-definite Hessian at the optimum.

nodes.name: Smoothness (8th-moment bounds and Hessian Lipschitz)
nodes.statement_clean: Eighth-moment gradient/Hessian bounds and Lipschitz Hessian on a neighborhood of $\theta^*$.

nodes.name: Strong smoothness (third-derivative Lipschitz)
nodes.statement:
For each $x$, $
abla^3 f(\cdot;x)$ is $M(x)$-Lipschitz: $\ltwo{(
abla^3 f(	heta;x) - 
abla^3 f(	heta';x))(u\otimes u)} \le M(x)\ltwo{	heta-	heta'}\ltwo{u}^2$ on $U$, with $\E[M(X)^8] \le M^8$.
nodes.statement_clean: Third derivatives of the loss are Lipschitz with eighth-moment bound on the Lipschitz constant.

nodes.name: Smoothness and Strong Convexity II (global, for SGD)
nodes.statement_clean: Global fourth-moment smoothness and strong convexity used for the SGD analysis.

nodes.name: Average mixture (AVGM)
nodes.statement: Distribute $N=mn$ samples evenly to $m$ machines; each computes its local empirical minimizer $\theta_{1,i}$; return $\bar\theta_1 = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m \theta_{1,i}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Compute local empirical minimizers and average them across machines.
input: Total dataset of $N = mn$ i.i.d. samples

nodes.name: Subsampled average mixture (SAVGM)
nodes.statement: Each machine $i$ subsamples $\lceil rn\rceil$ points from its local data, computes $\theta_{1,i}$ on the full local data and $\theta_{2,i}$ on the subsample; output the bias-corrected average $\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{SAVGM}} = (\bar\theta_1 - r\bar\theta_2)/(1-r)$.
nodes.statement_clean: AVGM with a bootstrap-style subsample correction for bias.
input: Total dataset of $N = mn$ samples and $m$ machines

nodes.name: Stochastic gradient descent with averaging (SGDAVGM)
nodes.statement: Each machine runs $n$ iterations of projected SGD with stepsize $\eta_t = c/(\lambda t)$ on its local data to produce $\theta'_i$; the algorithm returns $\bar\theta^n = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m \theta'_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Each machine runs SGD on its local data; outputs are averaged across machines.
input: Total dataset of $N=mn$ samples and $m$ machines

nodes.name: Two-stage SGD + gradient descent for approximate ERM
nodes.statement: Stage 1: Run $\order(\log^2(mn)/\rho^2)$ steps of SGD on $F_1$ to enter the local strong-convexity ball $B_\rho(\theta_1)$. Stage 2: Run $\order(\log(mn))$ iterations of standard gradient descent to reach error $(mn)^{-2}$, total time $\order(n\log(mn))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Hybrid SGD-then-gradient-descent procedure achieving the $(mn)^{-2}$-accurate local minimizer in near-linear time.

nodes.name: Stochastic dual coordinate ascent (SDCA) baseline
nodes.statement: Run multiple passes of stochastic dual coordinate ascent on the regularized empirical objective; used as a near-oracle baseline in the ad-click experiment.
nodes.statement_clean: SDCA optimizer used as a comparison baseline.

nodes.name: Trust-region Newton via LIBSVM (local solver)
nodes.statement: Each local empirical minimizer $\theta_i$ in the ad-click experiment is computed using a trust-region Newton method implemented in LIBSVM.
nodes.statement_clean: Local-machine optimizer used to compute $\theta_{1,i}$ for AVGM/SAVGM.

nodes.name: Projected SGD update
nodes.statement: $\theta^{t+1/2} = \theta^t - \eta_t \nabla f(\theta^t; X_t)$ and $\theta^{t+1} = \arg\min_{\theta \in \Theta}\ltwo{\theta - \theta^{t+1/2}}^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: One-step projected stochastic gradient update.

nodes.name: Necessity of Hessian conditions (Bernoulli loss)
nodes.statement: With $X \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)$ and $f(\theta;x) = \theta^2 - \theta$ if $x=0$, else $\theta^2 \indic{\theta\le 0} + \theta$: $F_0$ is strongly convex and smooth but with discontinuous second derivative; $\E[\theta_{1,i}] = \Omega(n^{-1/2})$, so AVGM has MSE $\Omega(n^{-1})$.
nodes.statement_clean: A loss that satisfies first/second-order smoothness but has discontinuous Hessian, for which AVGM fails to beat the single-machine rate.

nodes.name: Synthetic regression simulations
nodes.statement: Three regression models (standard linear, cubic-misspecified, heteroskedastic) with $N = 100{,}000$, $d \in \{20, 40, 200\}$, and $m \in \{2,4,8,16,32,64,128\}$; least-squares loss; AVGM, SAVGM (with $r \in \{0.005,0.01,0.02,0.04\}$), SGDAVGM, single-machine, and oracle baselines compared.
nodes.statement_clean: Simulation study comparing AVGM, SAVGM, SGDAVGM, and baselines on three regression models.

nodes.name: Tencent SoSo ad-click experiment
nodes.statement: Five-fold validation on the Tencent {\tt soso.com} dataset ($N \approx 2.36 \times 10^8$, $d = 741{,}725$); evaluates AVGM, SAVGM ($r \in \{0.1, 0.25\}$) versus SDCA/SGD baselines on held-out log-loss and AUC; SAVGM outperforms AVGM as $m$ grows up to 128.
nodes.statement_clean: Real-world large-scale logistic regression experiment for advertisement click-through prediction.

nodes.name: AVGM mean-squared error bound
nodes.statement_clean: MSE of the AVGM estimator decays as $\sigma^2/(nm) + \order(n^{-2})$.
conclusions: Leading $\sigma^2/(nm)$ term matches centralized rate when $m \le \sqrt{N}$

nodes.name: SAVGM mean-squared error bound
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions 1--4, $\E[\ltwo{\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{SAVGM}} - \theta^*}^2] \le \frac{2+3r}{(1-r)^2}\cdot\frac{1}{nm}\sigma^2 + c(\frac{M^2 G^6}{\lambda^6} + \frac{G^4 H^2 d \log d}{\lambda^4})\frac{1}{r(1-r)^2}n^{-3} + \order(\frac{1}{(1-r)^2}m^{-1}n^{-2})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Subsampling correction reduces the bias-induced $n^{-2}$ term in AVGM to $n^{-3}$.
conclusions: Centralized first-order rate as long as $m < n^2$

nodes.name: SGDAVGM mean-squared error bound
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions 1 and 5, $\E[\ltwo{\bar\theta^n - \theta^*}^2] \le \frac{\alpha G^2}{\lambda^2 n m} + \frac{\beta^2}{n^{3/2}}$, where $\alpha = 4c^2$ and $\beta$ is the constant defined in the text.
nodes.statement_clean: Averaged-SGD MSE achieves the optimal $1/(nm)$ rate plus a $1/n^{3/2}$ bias term.
conclusions: Bias term $\beta^2/n^{3/2}$ dominates when $m$ is large

nodes.name: Hajek-Le Cam local asymptotic minimax theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: For any estimator $\widehat\theta_N$ based on $N$ i.i.d. samples, $\lim_{c\to\infty}\liminf_{N\to\infty}\sup_{\theta \in B_2(\theta^*, c/\sqrt N)} N\E_\theta[\ltwo{\widehat\theta_N - \theta}^2] \ge \tr(I(\theta^*)^{-1})$.
nodes.statement_clean: The trace of the inverse Fisher information lower-bounds the asymptotic minimax risk.
nodes.origin_citation: van der Vaart, Asymptotic Statistics 1998, Theorem 8.11

nodes.name: AVGM weak corollary (norm-based bound)
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem 1, $\E[\ltwo{\bar\theta - \theta^*}^2] \le \frac{2 G^2}{\lambda^2 nm} + \frac{c G^2}{\lambda^4 n^2}(L^2 \log d + H^2 G^2/\lambda^2) + \order(m^{-1}n^{-2}) + \order(n^{-3})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Easier-to-parse version of Theorem 1 obtained from operator-norm bounds on the inverse Hessian.

nodes.name: Maximum-likelihood Fisher-information bound
nodes.statement: If the loss is the negative log-likelihood for a parametric family, then under the conditions of Theorem 1, $\E[\ltwo{\bar\theta_1 - \theta^*}^2] \le \frac{2}{N}\tr(I(\theta^*)^{-1}) + \frac{c m^2 \tr(I(\theta^*)^{-1})}{\lambda^2 N^2}(L^2\log d + H^2 G^2/\lambda^2) + \order(m N^{-2})$.
nodes.statement_clean: For MLE, the AVGM leading term equals $2\tr(I^{-1})/N$, matching (up to a factor 2) the Hájek-Le Cam lower bound.

nodes.name: Good-events closeness
nodes.statement: On $\event_0\cap\event_1\cap\event_2$, $\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*} \le \frac{2\ltwo{\nabla F_1(\theta^*)}}{(1-\rho)\lambda}$ and $\nabla^2 F_1(\theta) \succeq (1-\rho)\lambda I$ for $\theta$ in the local ball.
nodes.statement_clean: Under the three good events, $F_1$ is locally strongly convex and its minimizer is close to $\theta^*$.

nodes.name: Moment consequences (gradient and Hessian deviation)
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical gradient and Hessian deviation moment bounds at $\theta^*$.

nodes.name: Higher-order moment of error
nodes.statement: For any $k \le \min\{k_1,k_2,k_3\}$: $\E[\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}^k] = \order(n^{-k/2}\frac{G^k}{(1-\rho)^k \lambda^k} + n^{-k_1/2} + n^{-k_2/2} + n^{-k_3/2}) = \order(n^{-k/2})$.
nodes.statement_clean: $k$th moment of $\theta_1-\theta^*$ scales as $n^{-k/2}$.

nodes.name: Higher-order matrix-moment bound
nodes.statement: For $k \le \min\{k_1,k_2,k_3\}/2$, $\E[\matrixnorm{Q}_2^k] = \order(n^{-k/2})$, where $Q = \nabla^2 F_1(\theta^*) - \nabla^2 F_1(\theta')$.
nodes.statement_clean: Operator norm moments of the Hessian-difference $Q$ scale as $n^{-k/2}$.

nodes.name: Bias bound for AVGM/SAVGM (target-norm-e)
nodes.statement: $\ltwo{\E[(\theta_1 - r\theta_2)/(1-r) - \theta^*]}^2 \le \order(1)\cdot \frac{1}{r(1-r)^2}(\frac{M^2 G^6}{\lambda^6} + \frac{G^4 H^2}{\lambda^4}d\log d) n^{-3}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bias of the SAVGM estimator decays as $n^{-3}$.

nodes.name: Variance bound for SAVGM (target-e-norm)
nodes.statement: $\E[\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^* - r(\theta_2 - \theta^*)}^2] \le (2+3r)\E[\ltwo{\nabla^2 F_0(\theta^*)^{-1}\nabla F_1(\theta^*)}^2] + \order(n^{-2})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Variance of the SAVGM combination is bounded by $(2+3r)$ times the asymptotic variance plus $\order(n^{-2})$.

nodes.name: First-level third-order expansion
nodes.statement_clean: Third-order Taylor expansion of the empirical-minimizer error around $\theta^*$ with $\order(n^{-3})$ remainder.

nodes.name: Second-level third-order expansion (subsampled)
nodes.statement_clean: Analogue of the first-level expansion for the subsampled estimator $\theta_2$.

nodes.name: SGD distance bound (Rakhlin-Shamir-Sridharan)
nodes.statement: If $\E[\ltwo{g_t}^2] \le G^2$ for all $t$ and $\eta_t = c/(\lambda t)$ with $c \ge 1$, then $\E[\ltwo{\theta^t - \theta^*}^2] \le \alpha G^2/(\lambda^2 t)$ where $\alpha = 4c^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sharp $1/t$ MSE rate for projected SGD with $1/t$ stepsize.

nodes.name: Vector Rosenthal inequality (de Acosta)
nodes.statement:
For independent random vectors $X_i$ in a separable Banach space with $\E[
orm{X_i}^k] < \infty$, there exists $C_k$ such that $\E[|
orm{\sum X_i} - \E
orm{\sum X_i}|^k] \le C_k[(\sum \E
orm{X_i}^2)^{k/2} + \sum \E
orm{X_i}^k]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Banach-space Rosenthal-type inequality for sums of independent random vectors.

nodes.name: Matrix Rosenthal inequality (Chen-Gittens-Tropp)
nodes.statement: For independent symmetrically distributed Hermitian random matrices $X_i \in \R^{d\times d}$, $\E[\matrixnorm{\sum X_i}^k]^{1/k} \le \sqrt{2e\log d}\matrixnorm{(\sum \E[X_i^2])^{1/2}} + 2e\log d (\E[\max_i \matrixnorm{X_i}^k])^{1/k}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Non-commutative matrix Rosenthal moment inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2 (maximum-likelihood)
nodes.statement_clean: Direct calculation rewriting Theorem 1 in terms of the inverse Fisher information.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Decompose $\E[\ltwo{\bar\theta - \theta^*}^2] \le \frac{1}{m}\E[\ltwo{\theta_1-\theta^*}^2] + \ltwo{\E[\theta_1-\theta^*]}^2$; control each term via Taylor expansion of $\nabla F_1$ and Lemmas 1--4.
nodes.statement_clean: Independence-plus-Taylor decomposition; second moment gives $1/(nm)$ term, bias gives $1/n^2$ term.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Decompose $\E[\ltwo{\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{SAVGM}} - \theta^*}^2]$ into bias-squared and variance pieces (Lemmas 5 and 6), then use the third-order expansions (Lemmas 7 and 8) to cancel the leading bias terms after subsampling correction.
nodes.statement_clean: Decompose into bias and variance; third-order Taylor expansions show bias drops to $n^{-3}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (SGDAVGM)
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 9 to bound $\E[\ltwo{\theta^n-\theta^*}^2]$ by $\alpha G^2/(\lambda^2 n)$; then via Taylor remainder $r_t$, Markov's inequality and induction, show $\ltwo{\E[\theta^n - \theta^*]} \le \beta/n^{3/4}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combine the Rakhlin-Shamir-Sridharan rate with a bias induction $a_{t+1} \le (1-c/t)a_t + b/t^{7/4}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (good-events)
nodes.statement: Use the triangle inequality with $\delta_\rho = \min\{\rho, \rho\lambda/(4H)\}$ to show $F_1$ is $(1-\rho)\lambda$-strongly convex on a ball; then strong convexity plus a bound on $\nabla F_1(\theta^*)$ implies $\theta_1$ is close to $\theta^*$.
nodes.statement_clean: Local strong convexity argument using triangle inequality and event $\event_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2 (moment-consequences)
nodes.statement: Apply the de Acosta vector Rosenthal inequality (LP6.10) to $\nabla F_1(\theta^*) = n^{-1}\sum_i \nabla f(\theta^*;X_i)$; symmetrize and apply the Chen-Gittens-Tropp matrix Rosenthal inequality (LP6.11) to the Hessian deviation.
nodes.statement_clean: Combine vector and matrix Rosenthal inequalities with Jensen's inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7 (first-level third-order expansion)
nodes.statement: Restrict to event $\event = \event_0\cap\event_1\cap\event_2$; iterate the second-order expansion of $\nabla F_1$ together with Lemmas 2--4 and Hölder's inequality to absorb fourth-order remainders into $\mathcal{R}_3$.
nodes.statement_clean: Iterated Taylor expansion + moment bounds.

nodes.name: Linear regression has $H = 0$
nodes.statement: Assumption 3 is mild: for linear and logistic regression with non-rank-deficient population covariance and bounded data moments, both smoothness and local strong convexity hold; in linear regression, $H = 0$.

nodes.name: Optimal subsampling rate $r$
nodes.statement: When $m < N^{2/3}$, the bound (Thm 2) is minimized by $r \propto C \sqrt{m}/n = C m^{3/2}/N$ with $C \approx (G^2/\lambda^2)\max\{MG/\lambda, H\sqrt{d\log d}\}$.

nodes.name: Allowed number of machines $m$
nodes.statement: AVGM allows $m \le N^{1/2}\sqrt{\lambda^2/\max\{L^2\log d, H^2 G^2/\lambda^2\}}$; SAVGM permits $m \le N^{2/3}(\lambda^2/\max\{MG/\lambda, H\sqrt{d\log d}\})^{2/3}$ for the optimal rate.

nodes.name: Multiple subsamples / with-replacement variants for SAVGM
nodes.statement: Open: does computing multiple subsamples per machine reduce variance or improve performance, and does using subsamples with replacement (vs. without replacement as analyzed) yield improved performance?
nodes.statement_clean: Whether richer resampling at each machine improves SAVGM is left open.

nodes.name: Bootstrap correction for SGDAVGM
nodes.statement: Open: it is unclear whether a bootstrap subsampling correction is possible for the stochastic-gradient-based estimator SGDAVGM to remove the $\beta^2/n^{3/2}$ bias term.
nodes.statement_clean: Can SAVGM-style bias correction be applied to SGDAVGM?

nodes.name: Decomposition methods for non-parametric estimation
nodes.statement: Open: nonparametric estimation problems often suffer superlinear scaling in dataset size; whether the AVGM/SAVGM-style decomposition strategies extend to such settings is an open avenue.
nodes.statement_clean: Extending averaging methods to non-parametric estimation is left for future work.

nodes.name: Compute local empirical minimizer on each machine
nodes.statement: For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$, processor $i$ computes $\theta_{1,i} \in \arg\min_{\theta \in \Theta} \frac{1}{|S_{1,i}|}\sum_{x \in S_{1,i}} f(\theta; x)$.

nodes.name: Average the local minimizers
nodes.statement: Compute $\bar\theta_1 = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m \theta_{1,i}$ and return.

nodes.name: Subsample on each machine
nodes.statement: Each processor $i$ draws $S_{2,i}$ of size $\lceil rn\rceil$ uniformly at random without replacement from $S_{1,i}$.

nodes.name: Compute both empirical minimizers per machine
nodes.statement: Each processor $i$ computes $\theta_{1,i}$ on $S_{1,i}$ and $\theta_{2,i} \in \arg\min_{\theta \in \Theta} \frac{1}{|S_{2,i}|}\sum_{x \in S_{2,i}} f(\theta; x)$ on the subsample.

nodes.name: Form bias-corrected combination
nodes.statement: Compute $\bar\theta_2 = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m \theta_{2,i}$ and return $\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{SAVGM}} = (\bar\theta_1 - r\bar\theta_2)/(1-r)$.

nodes.name: Run $n$ iterations of projected SGD on each machine
nodes.statement: Each machine performs $n$ iterations of projected SGD with stepsize $\eta_t = c/(\lambda t)$ on its local data of size $n$, producing $\theta'_i$.

nodes.name: Average the local SGD outputs
nodes.statement: Return $\bar\theta^n = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m \theta'_i$.

nodes.name: Stage 1: SGD warm-up to enter local strong-convexity ball
nodes.statement: Perform $\order(\log^2(mn)/\rho^2)$ iterations of SGD on $F_1$ to obtain a point inside $B_\rho(\theta_1)$ with high probability.

nodes.name: Stage 2: standard gradient descent refinement
nodes.statement: Run $\order(\log(mn))$ iterations of standard gradient descent under local strong convexity to drive squared error down to $(mn)^{-2}$; total time $\order(n\log(mn))$.

nodes.name: Decompose averaged-error into variance and squared-bias terms
nodes.statement: By independence of $\theta_i$ across machines: $\E[\ltwo{\bar\theta - \theta^*}^2] \le \frac{1}{m}\E[\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}^2] + \ltwo{\E[\theta_1 - \theta^*]}^2$ (eq. (eqn:error-inequality)).

nodes.name: Define good events and apply Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Define $\event = \event_0 \cap \event_1 \cap \event_2$ from (eqn:good-events). Lemma 1 (LP6.1) gives $\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*} \le 2\ltwo{\nabla F_1(\theta^*)}/((1-\rho)\lambda)$ on $\event$; Lemma 2 (LP6.2) bounds $\P(\event^c)$ by union bound.

nodes.name: Control $\E[\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}^2]$ via Taylor expansion
Control $\ltwo{\E[\theta_1 - \theta^*]}^2$ via recursive expansion
nodes.statement: It remains to bound the squared bias. Recursively substitute the expansion to obtain $\theta_1 - \theta^* = v + \indic{\event^c}(\theta_1 - \theta^* - v)$ with $\E[v]$ involving $\E[H^{-1}(P+Q)H^{-1}\nabla F_1(\theta^*)]$, then bound this by $C(L^2\log d + H^2 G^2/\lambda^2)\E[\ltwo{H^{-1}\nabla F_1(\theta^*)}^2]/(\lambda^2 n) + \order(n^{-3})$.

nodes.name: Combine variance and bias bounds
nodes.statement: Plugging the bounds from steps 3 and 4 back into the decomposition (step 1) yields the theorem statement, with the leading term $\frac{2}{nm}\E[\ltwo{H^{-1}\nabla f(\theta^*;X)}^2]$ and second-order correction $\frac{c}{\lambda^2 n^2}(L^2\log d + H^2 G^2/\lambda^2)\E[\ldots]$ plus lower-order remainders.

nodes.name: Set up bias-variance decomposition for the SAVGM combination
nodes.statement: Write $\E[\ltwo{(\bar\theta_1 - r\bar\theta_2)/(1-r) - \theta^*}^2] \le \ltwo{\E[(\theta_1 - r\theta_2)/(1-r) - \theta^*]}^2 + \frac{1}{m}\E[\ltwo{(\theta_1 - r\theta_2)/(1-r) - \theta^*}^2]$ (eq. (eqn:bootstrap-decomposition)).

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 5 (target-norm-e) for the squared bias
nodes.statement: By Lemma 5 (LP6.5), the squared bias of the SAVGM combination is $\le \order(1)\frac{1}{r(1-r)^2}(M^2 G^6/\lambda^6 + G^4 H^2 d\log d/\lambda^4)n^{-3}$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 6 (target-e-norm) for the variance term
nodes.statement: By Lemma 6 (LP6.6), the variance term is bounded by $(2+3r)\E[\ltwo{H^{-1}\nabla F_1(\theta^*)}^2] + \order(n^{-2})$.

nodes.name: Combine the two lemmas to conclude
nodes.statement: Summing the bounds from steps 2 and 3 in the decomposition of step 1 yields the theorem's bound: $\frac{2+3r}{(1-r)^2 m}\sigma^2 + \order(\frac{1}{(1-r)^2}m^{-1}n^{-2}) + \order(\frac{1}{r(1-r)^2}n^{-3})$.

nodes.name: Reduce to per-machine bounds via independence inequality
nodes.statement: By (eqn:error-inequality): $\E[\ltwo{\bar\theta^n - \theta^*}^2] \le \frac{1}{m}\E[\ltwo{\theta^n - \theta^*}^2] + \ltwo{\E[\theta^n - \theta^*]}^2$. It suffices to prove (a) $\E[\ltwo{\theta^n - \theta^*}^2] \le \alpha G^2/(\lambda^2 n)$ and (b) $\ltwo{\E[\theta^n - \theta^*]}^2 \le \beta^2/n^{3/2}$.

nodes.name: Variance bound via Lemma 9 (Rakhlin-Shamir-Sridharan)
nodes.statement: Lemma 9 (LP6.9) gives part (a) directly: $\E[\ltwo{\theta^t - \theta^*}^2] \le \alpha G^2/(\lambda^2 t)$ with $\alpha = 4c^2$.

nodes.name: Bias recursion via Taylor remainder $r_t$
nodes.statement: Decompose $g_t = \nabla f_t(\theta^*) + \nabla^2 f_t(\theta^*)(\theta^t - \theta^*) + r_t$ and bound $\E[\ltwo{r_t}]$ via Markov's inequality and Assumption 5; obtain $\ltwo{\E[\theta^{t+1} - \theta^*]} \le (1 - c/t)\ltwo{\E[\theta^t - \theta^*]} + b/t^{7/4}$ for $t \ge \tau_0$.

nodes.name: Inductive argument $a_t \le \beta/t^{3/4}$
nodes.statement: By induction on $t$ with $\beta = \max\{\tau_0 R, b/(c-1)\}$: assuming $a_t \le \beta/t^{3/4}$, the recursion of step 3 gives $a_{t+1} \le \beta(t-1)/t^{7/4} - (\beta(c-1) - b)/t^2 \le \beta/(t+1)^{3/4}$. Setting $t = n$ proves part (b).

nodes.name: Establish $(1-\rho)\lambda$-strong convexity of $F_1$ on $U$
nodes.statement:
For $	heta \in U = \{\ltwo{	heta - 	heta^*} < \delta_ho\}$, triangle inequality gives $\matrixnorm{
abla^2 F_1(	heta) - 
abla^2 F_0(	heta^*)}_2 \le H\ltwo{	heta - 	heta^*} + ho\lambda/2$ on $\event_1$. Choosing $\delta_ho \le ho\lambda/(4H)$ gives $
abla^2 F_1(	heta) \succeq (1-ho)\lambda I$.

nodes.name: Suppose $\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*} > \delta_\rho$ for contradiction
nodes.statement: Strong convexity on $U$ yields $\min\{\interp\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}, \delta_\rho^2/(\interp\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*})\} < 2\ltwo{\nabla F_1(\theta^*)}/((1-\rho)\lambda) \le \delta_\rho$ for any $\interp \in (0,1)$. Suppose for contradiction $\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*} > \delta_\rho$ and set $\interp = \delta_\rho/\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}$ to obtain $\delta_\rho < \delta_\rho$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Conclude bound on $\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}$
nodes.statement: Therefore $\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*} \le \delta_\rho$, and the strong-convexity inequality with $\theta' = \theta_1$ yields $\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}^2 \le \frac{2\ltwo{\nabla F_1(\theta^*)}}{(1-\rho)\lambda}\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}$. Dividing by $\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}$ completes the proof.

nodes.name: Gradient bound via vector Rosenthal (de Acosta)
nodes.statement:
Apply Lemma 10 (LP6.10) to $

abla f(	heta^*;X_i)$ with Jensen's inequality to bound $\E[\ltwo{
abla F_1(	heta^*)}^k] \le C G^k / n^{k/2}$, proving (eqn:grad-bound).

nodes.statement:
Define $Z_i =  rac{1}{n}(
abla^2 f(	heta^*;X_i) - 
abla^2 F_0(	heta^*))$, symmetrize via Rademacher variables, and apply Lemma 11 (LP6.11) to obtain $\E[\matrixnorm{\sum Z_i}^k]^{1/k} \le 5\sqrt{\log d}\matrixnorm{(n^{-1}\E[(
abla^2 f(	heta^*;X) - 
abla^2 F_0(	heta^*))^2])^{1/2}} + 4e\log d \cdot n^{(1-k)/k}L$, proving (eqn:hessian-bound).

nodes.name: Restrict to good event $\event$
nodes.statement: By (eqn:no-bad-events), $\E[\indic{\event^c}\ltwo{\theta_1 - \theta^*}^2] = \order(R^2 n^{-4})$, so it suffices to prove the expansion on $\event = \event_0 \cap \event_1 \cap \event_2$.

abla F_1(	heta^*) - H^{-1}(

abla^3 F_1(	heta^*)(\Delta\otimes\Delta) + H^{-1}(

abla^3 F_1(	heta'))(\Delta\otimes\Delta)$ (eq. (eqn:third-order-taylor-expansion)).
